claim: An automatic compiler can generate correct and competitive modular residue sieves for structured families k*b^n+c.
An adaptive sieve bound can improve end-to-end time or energy on at least some regimes.
Automatic engine routing can remain within 3 percent of the best measured static engine on held-out workloads.
An asynchronous CPU/GPU pipeline can reduce idle time and total processing time on target workloads.
Generic fixed-size CUDA modular arithmetic can beat CPU GMP/FLINT end-to-end on sufficiently large uniform batches.
Proof integration from the start can reduce recalculation and validation risk at acceptable total cost.
A portfolio scheduler using frequent intermediate signals can improve a selected objective over fixed allocation.
The combination of a family language, congruence compilation, routing, and certification can constitute a distinct contribution.
primesieve 12.15 implements the audited segmented wheel and bucket architecture and passes its supplied local MSVC tests.
GMP 6.3.0 provides the audited multiprecision CPU arithmetic baseline under per-component dual licensing.
FLINT 3.6.0 contains documented and source-located machine-word, PRP, APRCL and rigorous primality paths.
Prime95 30.19 provides audited FFT-based Mersenne LL and PRP workflows, error controls, checkpoints and PRP proof files under a custom EULA.
evidence: audits/prime95-gwnum.md; official source and binary archives

claim: The pinned gpuowl PRPLL, Frey-PRPLL and Mlucas sources provide distinct external Mersenne implementation paths, none locally reproduced in stage 2.
The pinned OpenPFGW mirror supports structured-form PRP through a composite distribution whose licensing prevents redistribution without further review.
The pinned Genefer22 source implements specialized generalized-Fermat CPU/OpenCL tests and a documented proof workflow.
PARI/GP 2.17.4 source contains rigorous primality selection, Pocklington-Lehmer, APRCL/ECPP, certificate generation and validation paths.
GMP-ECM 7.0.7 is an audited factoring tool and is not a primality test.
CGBN is a beta CUDA fixed-size big-integer reference limited to documented group and bit-size ranges, not a giant FFT/NTT engine.
PRST 14.0 has broad documented Proth/Riesel capabilities but lacks an unambiguous project-wide license grant and is not selectable for integration.
The mandatory Proth/Riesel search found PRST, LLR2, proth20, NewPGen, srsieve, sr2sieve and PSieve-CUDA, with unresolved modern licensed-sieve coverage documented explicitly.
Algorithm-selection and portfolio literature motivates later experiments but does not validate PrimeForge hypothesis H3.
